{{Short description|US Department of State project}}{{Infobox award|name=YSEALI|image=YSEALI_5th_Year_Anniversary_Logo.png|sponsor=[[Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs]] ([[United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State]])|established=December 2013|website=http://yseali.state.gov|eligibility=18-35 years old from [[Timor Leste]] or any [[ASEAN]] country|subheader=Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative|awarded_for=Outstanding work and potentials as emerging leader from [[Southeast Asia]]|motto=Never Too Young To Lead|related=[[Young African Leaders Initiative]], [[Fulbright Scholarship]], [[United States Cultural Exchange Programs]]|location=[[United States of America]]|image caption=YSEALI's 5th year anniversary logo in 2018}}

The '''Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative''', also known as '''YSEALI''' (pronounced {{IPAc-en|w|aɪ|ˈ|s|iː|l|i}}), is a highly-competitive [[United States Cultural Exchange Programs|cultural exchange program]] for [[Southeast Asia|Southeast Asian]] emerging leaders sponsored by the [[United States Department of State|U.S.]] [[Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs|Bureau of Education and Cultural Affairs]]. YSEALI programs are known to have 1-2% acceptance rates and are usually awarded to emerging leaders with outstanding work and potentials in their chosen fields or advocacies.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}}

The initiative was launched by President [[Barack Obama]] in Manila in December 2013<ref>{{cite web |title=FACT SHEET: The President's Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative |url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2013/12/03/fact-sheet-president-s-young-southeast-asian-leaders-initiative |website=Obama White House |date=3 December 2013 |publisher=Office of the Press Secretary |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> as a way to strengthen leadership development, networking, and cultural exchange among emerging leaders within the age range of 18 to 35 years old<ref>{{cite web |title=About YSEALI |url=https://asean.usmission.gov/yseali/yseali-about/ |website=U.S. Mission to ASEAN |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> from the 10 member-states of the [[Association of Southeast Asian Nations]] and [[Timor Leste]]. YSEALI's programs include prestigious exchange fellowship programs to the [[United States]], [[Postgraduate diploma|professional short courses and diplomas]], virtual and on-ground workshops within [[Southeast Asia]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Asia Foundation Announces Participants of YSEALI Regional Workshop on Future Workforce |url=https://asiafoundation.org/2021/03/28/asia-foundation-announces-participants-of-yseali-regional-workshop-on-future-workforce/ |access-date=23 April 2021 |agency=The Asia Foundation}}</ref> and [[Grant (money)|seed grant]] funding opportunities. 

The programs fall under the key core themes of [[civic engagement]], [[sustainable development]], [[economic development]], [[governance]], and the [[environmentalism|environment]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Institute Themes |url=https://www.ysealipfp.org/themes |website=YSEALI Professional Fellows Program |publisher=Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> 

Alumni of YSEALI programs later assume key positions in government, civil societies, and corporations after their programs. Notable alumni of YSEALI include [[Vico Sotto]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Vico Sotto chosen as one of 12 global anti-corruption champions |agency=SunStar Philippines |url=https://www.sunstar.com.ph/article/1886934/Manila/Local-News/Vico-Sotto-chosen-as-one-of-12-global-anti-corruption-champions |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> [[Syed Saddiq]], [[Carrie Tan]], and [[Lee Chean Chung]]. As of September 2020, the program has more than 5,000 alumni and 150,000 members across member countries.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-10|title=[FACT SHEET] Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative (YSEALI)|url=https://asean.usmission.gov/fact-sheet-young-southeast-asian-leaders-initiative-yseali/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=U.S. Mission to ASEAN|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, [[Texas]] representative [[Joaquin Castro]] filed a bill in the [[United States House of Representatives|US House of Representatives]] to strengthen YSEALI as a law.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reps. Castro and Tenney Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Support the Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative {{!}} U.S. Congressman Joaquin Castro|url=https://castro.house.gov/media-center/press-releases/reps-castro-and-tenney-introduce-bipartisan-bill-to-support-the-young-southeast-asian-leaders-initiative|access-date=2021-08-01|website=castro.house.gov|language=en}}</ref>

== YSEALI Academic Fellowships ==

The YSEALI Academic Fellowship Program which brings the participating delegation<ref>{{cite news |title=UTM Postgrad Student Sole Malaysian Representative at the YSEALI Academic Fellowship Program |url=https://news.utm.my/2016/03/utm-postgrad-student-is-the-only-malaysian-academic-fellow-representative-at-the-yseali-academic-fellowship-program/ |access-date=23 April 2021 |agency=UTM NewsHub |publisher=Universiti Teknologi Malaysia}}</ref> from each Southeast Asian country to study in an academic institution in the United States for six weeks to learn about their chosen advocacy,<ref>{{cite news |title=Thai Fellows of Spring 2019 YSEALI Academic Fellowships Visit the Embassy |url=https://thaiembdc.org/2019/06/12/thai-fellows-of-spring-2019-yseali-academic-fellowships-visit-the-embassy/ |access-date=23 April 2021 |agency=Royal Thai Embassy, Washington D.C. |archive-date=23 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423200414/https://thaiembdc.org/2019/06/12/thai-fellows-of-spring-2019-yseali-academic-fellowships-visit-the-embassy/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> comparable to the [[Young African Leaders Initiative]]'s Mandela Washington Fellowship program.

Institutions that have hosted the Academic Fellowship Program are the following:
* [[Arizona State University]]<ref>{{cite news |title=ASU hosts 2018 Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative fellows |url=https://news.asu.edu/20180403-asu-hosts-2018-young-southeast-asian-leaders-institutes |access-date=23 April 2021 |agency=Arizona State University}}</ref>
* [[Brown University]]<ref>{{cite web |title=YSEALI at Brown University |url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/college/swearer/programs/yseali-brown-university/229 |website=Brown University |publisher=Swearer Center |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Emily |title=Swearer Center, UConn to foster leadership skills in Southeast Asian fellows |url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/2018/09/16/swearer-center-uconn-foster-leadership-skills-southeast-asian-fellows/ |access-date=23 April 2021 |publisher=Brown Daily Herald}}</ref>
* [[East-West Center]]
* [[Kennesaw State University]]
* [[Northern Illinois University]]
* [[Portland State University]]
* [[Temple University]]
* [[University of Connecticut]]
* [[University of Montana]]
* [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]
* [[University of Nebraska Omaha]]
*[[University of Texas at Austin]]

== YSEALI Seeds for the Future ==
The YSEALI Seeds for the Future is a small grants competition for youth-led innovative projects in Southeast Asia established by the [[United States Department of State|U.S. Mission to ASEAN]], as implemented by [[Cultural Vistas]]. Since its establishment in 2017, the YSEALI Seeds for the Future has provided funding to 100 youth-led projects within the [[ASEAN|ASEAN region]] and [[East Timor|Timor Leste]] funding at most US$15,000 for each successful winner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=YSEALI Seeds for the Future |url=https://culturalvistas.org/our-programs/yseali-seeds/ |access-date=2021-08-02 |website=Cultural Vistas |language=en}}</ref>
